target_customer: Medical clinics (starting with urology) that pay a flat per-scan fee
problem: MRI cancer screening needs multimillion dollar systems and expert operation, so most sites cannot offer it.
business_model: Owned mobile MRI units with flat per-scan fee (service model)
product_category: Mobile compact MRI for cancer screening

founders.name: Efrain Torres
founders.background_notes: Trained as biomedical engineer; about six years developing MRI methods with patents per YC page

competitors.name: Hyperfine
competitors.what: FDA cleared portable ultra-low-field brain MRI (Swoop)

competitors.name: Ezra
competitors.what: Elective full-body MRI screening, aims for 15 minute $500 scan in 2026

technical_complexity.rationale: New MRI physics, algorithms and hardware plus FDA clearance are needed.

defensibility.rationale: Two patents are cited by YC page and FDA clearance would be a barrier; not yet obtained.

market_need_then: Early detection improves outcomes; company reports six clinics signed, $12.75M in letters of intent and a $30k deposit (self-reported).

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; name resembles Spanish adelante (forward) but no source states the origin.

outcome_analysis: Adialante is a Spring 2026 company still pre-clearance, with no FDA approval reported and its first units expected in clinics around Q4 2026. Its story rests on a hard technical and regulatory path, grant support and letters of intent; it is too early to assign outcome factors.
notes: UNVERIFIED: a 2024 profile reportedly says $1.5M seed from University of Minnesota, state of Minnesota, NSF and angels; one source says a $2M SBIR was paused for nine months. Locations conflict (San Francisco on YC page, Minneapolis in press). Founding year not found. Name origin not found.
